chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed Zaynab bint Jahash said, 'Does the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) think that if he were to free our way, we would not find a husband other than him?' And he had detached from his wives for twenty-nine nights.

So when Zaynab said what she said, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Jibra'il to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so he said, 'Say to your wives: If you desire the life of the world and its adornment, then come, I will give you a provision' – both the two Verses.
So they said, 'But we choose Allah and His Messenger and the House of the Hereafter'.

key_terms.زَيْنَبُ بِنْتَ جَحْشٍ: Zaynab bint Jahash, one of the Prophet's wives

ai.seo_question: What was the reason for the Prophet's detachment from his wives and what was the outcome of the choice offered to them?
ai.summary: This hadith details the event of Izl (detachment) where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) separated from his wives for twenty-nine nights, prompting Zaynab bint Jahash to question their fidelity. The subsequent revelation commanded the wives to choose between worldly comfort and the Hereafter, a choice they affirmed by selecting Allah and His Messenger, thereby establishing their spiritual precedence in Shia tradition.
